text:
diego: Heads up — after the kernel-selector change (rti@c3f9e) we see a 10–18% P95 latency regression on Qwen2.5 8k workloads. Flamegraphs attached. Repro: ./scripts/profile_qwen2p5.sh --seq 8192 --batch 4. Happens on both A100 and H100 clusters. Any pointers?

sam: Can you paste the profiler output (CUDA vs CPU) + the kernel selector log? Is batching behavior different or is it specifically KV/attn kernel choice?

diego: Pasting relevant slice from the profiler + selector log: ```
# torch profiler (summary)
CUDA ops: attention_fwd fused_attn_v2: 42%
CUDA ops: aten::bmm (fallback): 18%
CUDA ops: memcpy H2D/D2H: 9%
CPU ops: kernel_selector: evaluate 1.6s

# kernel_selector.log
[INFO] kernels evaluated: fused_attn_v2 (lat=12.3ms), cuBLAS_gemm_fp16_v2 (lat=13.1ms), generic_biggemm (lat=18.9ms)
[WARN] chosen kernel: generic_biggemm for KV due to kv_head_mismatch (kv_heads=16, attn_heads=32)
```
That kv_head_mismatch line looks suspicious — model conf has attn_heads=32, kv_heads=16 (Qwen2.5 uses grouped-kv). We used a reshaping path that expects equal heads; selector falls back to slower generic kernel.

marie: Noted. Also saw tokenizer oddness in the same runs: multilingual tokenization for ja/zh returns very long sequences with <special> splits which explode padding and reduce effective batching. Example: some Japanese inputs produce 6–10% extra tokens due to different tokenization of punctuation. Suggest per-language batch-size cap or dynamic per-example truncation before batching.

izzy: I ran a focused microbench to isolate the slow path. When kv_heads != attn_heads we hit codepath: fused_attn_v2 -> fails kernel precondition -> fallback to aten::bmm + extra permutes. Rough numbers: fused_attn_v2: 11.8ms; fallback sequence: permute+reshape+aten::bmm+memcpy = 16.5ms. Full trace: ```
(1) ln.kv_proj: [B, L, kv_heads, head_dim] expected layout
(2) code tried to use contiguous view with heads==kv_heads assert -> assert fails -> convert with .reshape + .contiguous -> extra memcpy
```
Patch idea: add a fused kernel variant that accepts grouped-kv layout (kv_heads divisor of attn_heads) and update kernel_selector precondition to prefer it. I sketched a patch: ```
// pseudo
if (kv_heads != attn_heads && (attn_heads % kv_heads == 0)) return fused_attn_grouped_kv;
```

sam: Good. Also circle back to rope vs ALiBi: did anything change in the model config? The selector may be choosing kernels incompatible with scaled RoPE which forces per-head scaling and changes q/k layout.

diego: Yes — in the model card we added rope_scaling=0.87 for Qwen2.5 to stabilize long-range bias. kernel_selector currently only checks rope_type (RoPE vs ALiBi) but not rope_scaling value. When rope_scaling != 1.0 some kernels that assume unit-scale produce incorrect results and get disabled; selector then picks slower fallback. For a quick experiment I forced ALiBi compatible kernels and perf returned to within ~1–2% of baseline.

marie: For the tokenizer edgecases, short-term mitigation: clamp max_tokens_per_example by language mapping (e.g., ja: 6000, en: 8192, zh: 7000) before batching. Longer-term: evaluate tokenizers with byte-level fallback to reduce weird splits.

izzy: Agree. Also noticed a memory regression on KV cache growth in long-chat runs — when grouped-kv path did reshape+contiguous we temporarily allocate 1.5x memory. On memory-constrained Dedicated nodes that triggered OOM-ish GC and latency spikes. Adding the grouped fused kernel removes that extra allocation.

diego: Quick checklist: 1) add fused_attn_grouped_kv kernel variant (izzy owning) 2) update kernel_selector to prefer grouped variant for divisible heads (sam owning) 3) add rope_scaling check in selector and map to kernels that support scaled RoPE (diego owning) 4) apply tokenizer per-lang clamp and run regression harness (marie owning).

sam: For reproducible profiling, run: ```bash
./scripts/profile_qwen2p5.sh --seq 8192 --batch 4 --lang ja --trace /tmp/trace.json
python -m torch.profiler --profile /tmp/trace.json --flamegraph /tmp/flame.svg
```
Also add `--kernel-log DEBUG` to capture selection decisions.

deploy-bot: deploy rti@c3f9e — rolled back to rti@b1d2c after perf alerting (auto-rollback).

diego: Thanks. I'll open three PRs: grouped-kv kernel (w/ microbench), selector changes, and rope_scaling selector guard. Will link perf numbers in PRs.

marie: I'll add language-cap map to batching service and run on dev cluster.

izzy: I'll prototype grouped kernel this afternoon. If anyone can share link to the flamegraphs I posted earlier (private link expired), re-upload them here.

sam: I'll update regression dashboard to add a qwen2.5 long-seq test (ja/zh mix) and add alert for >5% P95 regression.

diego: TL;DR: regression is kernel-selection + kv-head mismatch + rope_scaling oversight + tokenizer-induced longer sequences. Multi-pronged fix in flight.

sam: :thumbsup: keep me posted and ping if you want a 30m pairing session.
